questions.q:
At the sea level, the dry air mass percentage composition is given as nitrogen gas : 70.0, oxygen gas : 27.0 and argon gas : 3.0. If total pressure is 1.15 atm , then calculate the ratio of followings respectively :
(i) partial pressure of nitrogen gas to partial pressure of oxygen gas
(ii) partial pressure of oxygen gas to partial pressure of argon gas
(Given : Molar mass of $\mathrm{N}, \mathrm{O}$ and Ar are 14, 16, and $40 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}$ respectively)
questions.solution:
$\frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{N}_2}}{\mathrm{Po}_2}=\frac{\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{N}_2} \cdot \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}}{\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{O}_2} \cdot \mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{T}}}=\frac{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{N}_2}}{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{O}_2}}$ {using Dalton's law of partial pressure}
$\begin{aligned} & =\frac{70 / 28}{27 / 32}=2.96 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{O}_2}}{\mathrm{P}_{\mathrm{Ar}}}=\frac{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{O}_2}}{\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{Ar}}}=\frac{27 / 32}{3 / 40}=11.25\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Three bulbs are filled with CH4, CO2 and Ne as shown in the picture. The bulbs are connected through pipes of zero volume. When the stopcocks are opened and the temperature is kept constant throughout, the pressure of the system is found to be______ atm. (Nearest integer).
questions.solution:
The total number of moles remains constant.

${n}_{1} + {n}_{2} + {n}_{3} = {n}_{f}$

${n}_{1}, {n}_{2}, {n}_{3}$ moles of gases in the individual containers. ${n}_{f}$ is resultant moles.

Using ideal gas equation $PV = nRT$, we van write as

$\dfrac{{P}_{1}{V}_{1}}{RT} + \dfrac{{P}_{2}{V}_{2}}{RT} + \dfrac{{P}_{3}{V}_{3}}{RT} = \dfrac{{P}_{f}{V}_{f}}{RT}$

${P}_{1}{V}_{1} + {P}_{2}{V}_{2} + {P}_{3}{V}_{3} = {P}_{f}{V}_{f}$

$2 \times 2 + 4 \times 3 + 3 \times 4 = {P}_{f} \times 9$

${P}_{f} = \dfrac{28}{9} \approx 3$

For $1mol$ of gas, the plot of $pV$ vs $p$ is shown below. p is the pressure and $V$ is the volume of the gas.

What is the value of compressibility factor at point $A$?
questions.solution:
According to Van der Waals equation,

$( P + \dfrac{a}{{{V}_{m}}^{2}} ) ( {V}_{m} - b ) = RT$

Where, ${V}_{m}$ = molar volume of the gas

$R$= Universal gas constant

$T$ = Temperature

$P$ = Pressure

At point A 'a' is considerable and 'b' is negligible.

So, $( P + \dfrac{a}{{{V}_{m}}^{2}} ) {V}_{m} = RT$

${PV}_{m} + \dfrac{a}{{V}_{m}} = RT$

Compressibility factor ($Z$) = $1 - \dfrac{a}{{V}_{m}RT}$

Hence, the correct answer is $1 - \dfrac{a}{RTV}$

questions.q:
The number of statement's, which are correct with respect to the compression of carbon dioxide from point (a) in the Andrews isotherm from the following is _________.

A. Carbon dioxide remains as a gas upto point (b)
B. Liquid carbon dioxide appears at point (c)
C. Liquid and gaseous carbon dioxide coexist between points (b) and (c)
D. As the volume decreases from (b) to (c), the amount of liquid decreases
questions.solution:
Andrews noticed that at high temperatures isotherms look like that of an ideal gas and the gas cannot be liquefied even at very high pressure. As the temperature is lowered, shape of the curve changes and data shows considerable deviation from ideal behaviour.

Carbon dioxide remains as a gas only up to point $b$.

At point $b$, liquid of a particular volume appears. Further compression does not change the pressure. Liquid and gaseous carbon dioxide coexist and further application of pressure results in the condensation of more gas until the point $c$ is reached. At point $c$, all the gas has been condensed and further application of pressure merely compresses the liquid as shown by steep line. A point like $d$ represents liquid state

questions.q: for a real gas at $25 ° C$ temperature and high pressure ($99$ bar) the value of compressibility factor is $2$, so the value of Van 1der Waal's constant '$b$' should be_____$\times {10}^{- 2}L{mol}^{- 1}$ (Given $R = 0 . 083L$ bar ${K}^{- 1}{mol}^{- 1}$)
questions.solution:
For real gas under high pressure we can neglect pressure corrections due to intermolecular forces. But since volume will be low, we can not neglect volume corrections due to molecular size.

$Z = 1 + \dfrac{Pb}{RT} = 2 ⇒ b = \dfrac{RT}{P}$

$= \dfrac{0 . 083 \times 298}{99}$

$= 0 . 25 \times {10}^{- 2}L{mol}^{- 1}$

questions.q: A mixture of hydrogen and oxygen contains $40 %$ hydrogen by mass when the pressure is $2 . 2$ bar. The partial pressure of hydrogen is bar.
questions.solution:
According to Dalton's law of partial pressures, the total pressure by a mixture of gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of each of the constituent gases.

${P}_{i} = {x}_{i}P{P}_{i} = partialpressureof{i}^{th}component . {x}_{i} = molefractionofthe{i}^{th}componentP = totalpressure$

Let ${W}_{{H}_{2}} = 40g ⇒ {n}_{{H}_{2}} = \dfrac{40}{2} = 20$

${W}_{{O}_{2}} = 60g ⇒ {n}_{{O}_{2}} = \dfrac{60}{32} = \dfrac{15}{8}$

${P}_{{H}_{2}} = \left(\dfrac{20}{20 + \dfrac{15}{8}}\right) \times 2 . 2$

$= \dfrac{20}{20 + 1 . 875} \times 2 . 2$

$= \dfrac{20}{21 . 875} \times 2 . 2$

$= 2 . 0114$

$≃ 2 . 01bar$

The pressure of a moist gas at $27 ° C$ is $4atm$. The volume of the container is doubled at the same temperature. The new pressure of the moist gas is $\ldots \times {10}^{- 1}$ atm. (Nearest integer)
(Given: The vapour pressure of water at $27 ° C$ is $0 . 4atm$)
questions.solution:
Dalton's Law states that the total pressure $P$ of moist air is the sum of partial pressures of dry air ${P}_{a}$ and water vapor ${P}_{v}$: $P = {P}_{a} + {P}_{v}$. Only the absolute pressure is the state parameter of moist air.

${P}_{gas} + {P}_{{H}_{2}O} = 4$

${P}_{gas} = 4 - 0 . 4 = 3 . 6atm$

As volume is doubled, ${\left[{P}_{gas}\right]}_{new} = 1 . 8atm$

New Total Pressure $= 1 . 8 + 0 . 4 = 2 . 2atm$
